United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Member States capacities strengthened in applying social and human scientific frontier knowledge to devise effective policy solutions to advance an inclusive development agenda with the aim to improve the well-being of people, particularly the most vulnerable, addressing the legacies of the pandemic crisis and face the social impact of climate change

description.narrative: The implementation strategy to deliver this output will be anchored in the Management of Social Transformations (MOST) programme, building on, and enhancing each of its three strategic pillars: research, intergovernmental, and knowledge brokering. MOST will focus on leveraging cooperation with social science and humanities communities to foster innovative knowledge production in areas relevant to UNESCO programmes, using existing modalities such as Chairs and Centres and new partnerships, with emphasis on connecting inequalities with emerging understandings of well-being and its multiple dimensions. Special attention will be given to the necessary changes to the intellectual underpinnings of the economic and social policy thinking of Member States to deliver better for people, particularly the most vulnerable. MOST will contribute to monitoring the Recommendation on Science and Scientific Researchers to support policy change and strengthen national innovation capacities. MOST will support policies and building capacities at national level and at sub-national level, including MOST Schools, Futures Literacy, and the Inclusive Policy Lab. MOST will continue to give particular attention to the humanities as essential intellectual and practical contributions to understanding of the contemporary world, through the contributions of history, philosophy, languages and literature and the artistic disciplines, that can assist critical and creative, to decision-making processes.
